modal.db_maint.help.flows_no_wp.steps:
With the check query, look at name, type and author of each flow.
If not needed, delete them: validations and links are removed automatically.
If one is needed, move it to an existing WP.
modal.db_maint.help.flows_no_wp.what: Flows whose work package has been deleted. They cannot be opened or linked.
modal.db_maint.help.folders_unused.steps:
With the check query (replace <ID>) look at name, parent folder and subfolders.
With FileZilla open on the server the folder with that name (under RA_Data, or inside the parent research folder) and check its contents.
If it is empty or the contents are not needed: run the fix query (subfolders first, then the folder) and delete the folder on disk.
If it contains needed files, leave it: the report remains but does no harm.
modal.db_maint.help.folders_unused.what: First-level (research project) or second-level (work package) folders not used by any research project or WP: usually leftovers of an interrupted creation or an old deletion. Each row matches a real folder on disk, under RA_Data.

modal.db_maint.help.models_no_wp.steps:
With the check query, look at name, folder and file of each model.
If not needed, delete them (the following cleaning removes links, authors, drawings and annotations).
If one is needed, move it to an existing WP and copy its files into a subfolder of that WP, then update folder and file from the Models dialog.
Check on the server the folders left by deleted WPs.

modal.db_maint.help.wp_no_research.steps:
With the check query, look at title and contents (objects, models, flows) of each WP.
If the WP is needed, assign it to an existing research project (query A, with the right res_id).
If not, delete it with its contents (query B).
On the server, with FileZilla, check the WP folder under RA_Data and delete it if no longer needed.
modal.db_maint.help.wp_no_research.what: Work packages whose research project has been deleted. Nobody can open them: to reach a WP you must enter its research project.
modal.db_maint.intro: Finds orphan records (rows pointing to research projects, work packages, objects, models, flows or users that no longer exist) and old data to remove periodically. “Analyze” changes nothing; “Clean” removes the rows of the checked items in a single operation recorded in the activity log.
